tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: three accounts of teams shipping product work with OpenAI models and Codex agents. It opened with two OpenAI customer stories, Merge using GPT-6 Astra and Codex for code review and Amplitude's Wave agent driving 1-2 day product changes.
whats_new: At QCon SF, OpenAI's Brian Yang said the ChatGPT ads product was built with Codex agents and no human-written code, held together by layered testing, sandboxes, and batched PR reviews.
why_it_matters: The first engineering account in the thread names the controls behind agent-written code (layered tests, sandboxes, batched review), where the customer stories only named the tools.

beats.headline: OpenAI customer stories pitch agents across the product loop
beats.summary: Published on OpenAI's own blog: Merge on code review and business tasks, Amplitude on an agent that picks, ships, and measures changes.

beats.headline: QCon SF talk details how OpenAI built ChatGPT ads with Codex agents
beats.summary: An independent InfoQ write-up of a conference talk, with the testing and review process rather than outcome claims.

open_questions: Does OpenAI publish defect or rollback rates for the agent-built ChatGPT ads codebase?
Does Amplitude report measured impact for changes shipped through its Wave agent?
Do teams outside OpenAI report the same no-human-code workflow working at production scale?
take_for_builders: Before letting coding agents merge unattended, put a sandboxed run and a layered test gate in front of every agent PR, and batch reviews rather than skipping them.
